Hi Samantha —

Great catching up last week. As discussed, I attached a draft addendum that:
- Extends the current MSA for 18 months (term alignment with your fiscal year)
- Adds a phased capacity onramp (20% month 1, 40% month 3, full uplift month 6)

Action items I’d like to confirm:
1) Can you confirm the onboarding date you’d prefer to target for the phased uplift?
2) Are there any procurement constraints (PO timing / signature authorities) we should plan for?

I’m looping Laura to flag any legal constraints on our side; Aditya for billing cadence. If you want, we can do a 30-min sync to walk the addendum and the mutual action plan.

Subject: Re: Renewal + Capacity onramp / proposed addendum v1

Diego —

Thanks for the draft. I’ve reviewed with Horizon Legal and attached our redlines. High-level notes:
- Term: We can agree to 18 months but request a 30-day termination for material data security failures.
- Capacity uplift: We need the phased percentages written as minimum guaranteed capacity per month, not estimated ramps.
- Audit logs: Require 12 months of immutable audit log storage and quarterly exportable reports.
- Liability: We propose to tighten the indemnity carveouts related to customer data processing; please see lines 52–64.

Two asks from our side:
1) Please confirm whether Redwood can commit to the minimum monthly throughput guarantee, and whether there are credit remedies if throughput is missed.
2) We’d like a 3rd-party SOC2 attestation appended (or confirmation that Redwood will provide the latest report before signature).

Attaching: Horizon_Addendum_v1_sarah-redlines.docx (docx) and a short Redline_Summary_HZN-47.pdf (pdf).

Laura / Aditya —

Forwarding Horizon’s redlines (attached). Sarah has requested: guaranteed monthly minimums for the phased uplift; a SOC2 attestation before signature; and a 30-day termination right for a material security failure.

Laura — can you:
- Review the indemnity tweak that Sarah flagged (lines 52–64) and propose alternative language we can live with?

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Wu <samantha.wu@horizontech.com>, Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@horizontech.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Dec 2029 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Horizon redlines — proposed counter language and next steps

Diego / Aditya —

Thanks for the ping and for sharing Horizon’s redlines. Quick read and proposed path below:

1) Indemnity / Liability (lines 52–64) - We cannot accept broad carveouts that remove customer data protections. Proposed counter: keep Redwood’s standard indemnity but narrow the scope to direct damages capped at the order value for the 12-month period (language attached). This preserves commercial balance while giving Horizon reasonable recourse.

2) Termination for security failure- 30-day cure is acceptable; we will keep materiality defined by the SOC2/control failure set. We’ll include a provision for remediation plan and an escalation path before termination.

3) Guaranteed minimums vs. phased ramp- Operationally, a hard minimum creates capacity reservation risk. Suggested compromise: a Minimum Committed Throughput (MCT) that converts to a billing credit if we miss sustained monthly MCT for 2 consecutive months. That gives Horizon predictability and protects Redwood from one-off spikes. Aditya — if you’re good with implementing a credit formula (e.g., 5% credit per missed month up to 20% cap), we can propose that.

4) SOC2 attestation- We can provide our 2028 SOC2 Type II report under an NDA. Recommend we link the report and include a clause: "Redwood will provide current SOC2 attestation within 10 business days of signature." That should satisfy compliance teams.

5) Execution flow- I propose we:
- Send a counter redline (I’ll draft) that accepts term length and termination cure, proposes the indemnity cap and MCT/credit approach, and confirms SOC2 delivery.
- Offer a 30-min legal+commercial sync with Horizon to walk the redline and the credit mechanics.
- If Horizon pushes back on MCT, we can offer a short-term pilot (60 days) with a one-time capacity reservation fee to bridge to full uplift.

I’ll attach proposed language for the indemnity cap and MCT credit schedule (word doc) and a redline copy for Diego to review before we send. Please confirm if we should include DocuSign links in the initial counter or wait until commercial terms are agreed.

Attachments: Laura_Counter_Redline_HZN-47.docx (docx), MCT_Credit_Term_Sheet.pdf (pdf)
